abstract: Wound healing assays are widely used to study fibroblast migration and proliferation in the lab. Although traditional scratch assays provide valuable insight, they can be time-intensive, inflexible, and difficult to reproduce. Computational models provide an efficient and reproducible way to study fibroblast behavior in silico. We developed an agent-based simulation of fibroblast scratch assays that models migration, proliferation, contact inhibition, cell-cell mechanical interactions, and the extracellular matrix (ECM) through a particle representation of fibroblasts and the ECM. To validate our model, we performed two tests: a leave-one-out test, where model parameters were calibrated to 6 imaging time series and tested on the remaining one, and a prediction test, where model parameters were calibrated to the first 24 hours of data and the remaining 66 hours of data were predicted. In our leave-one-out test, our model achieved a mean normalized root mean squared error (mean NRMSE) of 3.34%, and a Pearsons R of > 0.98 across all tested wound geometries time series. In the prediction test, the model predicted the remaining 66 hours of wound closure with an NRMSE of 2.08%. These results demonstrate that experimentally observed wound healing behavior of fibroblasts across different geometries can be modeled by local, agent-based rules. Our model provides an efficient platform for the experimentation and in silico study of fibroblast behavior.
